decisions.reason: The Trivital supplement range is a visibly branded line that builds on the firm's established pharmacy business, so dropping it would write off a public brand investment.
This skin and hair supplement was publicly launched as a new pharmacy offer within the Trivital brand, and weak sales can still be blamed on a competitive market phase.
The joint supplement was announced as new and given its own page, so it is part of the committed brand portfolio.
The immune supplement was promoted as the newest innovative Trivital product, and the pandemic-era interest in immunity supports keeping it.

The 2018 valsartan contamination problem can be attributed to an industry-wide temporary API issue, and a generic product fits the firm's broad generics strategy, although low investment and reputational damage make dropping it plausible.
The OTC triptan was given its own page and fits the stated push into consumer health products, so the firm is likely to keep backing it.
